assessments.reasoning: The GovData-branded government page contains the two language versions in its main content and identifies the Zero route. Its reported whole-page SHA-256 matches 942ff5fea9ce6e3184ff7c6134f259b06f901200211815e6ddd8ab7392254168.

The pinned Index scope expressly includes data licensing and distinguishes an identifiable grant from a dedication or related notice. The bilingual grant supplies the case-specific basis for applying that rule.

challenge.method: Checked the GovData origin, whole-page digest, both language blocks, embedded licence URL and provider metadata note. Tested substitution of the BY edition and classification of Zero as a public-domain dedication solely from its name.
challenge.results: The Zero title and explicit permission without conditions distinguish this instrument from Frankfurt’s attribution edition. The separate DCAT-AP.de instruction addresses providers recording a licence URI. It does not impose attribution on reusers. The text affirmatively grants use, which supports the License classification.

limitations: Active denotes the intended lifecycle mapping. Current Index admission, the licence selected for an individual dataset and installation eligibility require their own records.
The unrestricted-use language describes the grant in the identified instrument. The evidence does not establish the rights held by any particular provider.
reasoning: GovData publishes German and English Zero version 2.0 terms at data.gov.de/dl-de/zero-2-0. Both language blocks expressly permit use of the supplied data and metadata without restrictions or conditions and illustrate copying, modification, combination and integration. Under SCES §§1–3, the exact publisher representation establishes that description. The Index’s License criterion applies because the text makes an identifiable grant.
